label: Excel change alerts
text: I'm writing a Tampermonkey script that reads visible Excel cells and notifies me when something changes.

items.text: A Tampermonkey script that reads the Excel cells shown on screen
items.quote: Tampermonkey script that reads visible Excel cells

items.text: Get a notification when a value changes

concepts.term: userscript on the Excel web page
a watcher that can stop quietly

needs.reason: Only for work accounts with the workbook in OneDrive for Business or SharePoint: Microsoft's Office Scripts with Power Automate can check it on a schedule, even with the browser closed.

ntfy-push-alerts.why: You want the script to tell you when a cell changes. This gets that alert to your phone, not just the computer running Excel.
ntfy-push-alerts.how_it_helps: When the script spots a change, it sends a short message and your phone buzzes, even when you're away from the computer.
ntfy-push-alerts.do_you_need_it: Only if you want alerts on your phone. Tampermonkey can already show a desktop pop-up by itself.
ntfy-push-alerts.skip_if: Skip it if a pop-up on the same computer is enough, or alerts already go to a chat app you use.
ntfy-push-alerts.summary: ntfy: a free service that turns a simple web request from your script into a phone notification.

chrome-devtools-mcp.why: Your script reads cells from the Excel web page. The hard part is finding where Excel keeps those values on the page and seeing why the script misses them.
chrome-devtools-mcp.how_it_helps: Your AI can open the real Excel page, look at how the cells are built, try the reading code there and read the script's error messages.
chrome-devtools-mcp.do_you_need_it: Helpful while you write and debug the script. Without it, you copy the page's details to your AI by hand.
chrome-devtools-mcp.skip_if: Skip it if your AI tool can already open and read pages in your browser.
chrome-devtools-mcp.summary: The Chrome DevTools team's official add-on that lets your AI tool open, inspect and test pages in Chrome.

healthchecks-io.why: A watcher in a browser tab can stop quietly: the tab closes, the Microsoft sign-in expires, or Excel changes its page and the script finds no cells.
healthchecks-io.how_it_helps: The script checks in every few minutes. If the check-ins stop, you get an email, so silence never passes for nothing changing.
healthchecks-io.do_you_need_it: Useful later, once you rely on the alerts. The free plan covers up to 20 checks.
healthchecks-io.skip_if: Skip it if a silent stop costs you nothing.
healthchecks-io.summary: Healthchecks: a free monitor that tells you when the regular check-ins from your script stop arriving.
